questions.question:
In a binary tree with n nodes, every node has an odd number of descendants.
Every node is considered to be its own descendant. What is the number of nodes
in the tree that have exactly one child?

If a node had exactly one child, its descendants = itself + child's descendants = 1 + odd = even, which contradicts the condition.

So no node has exactly one child.

Answer: 0

questions.question:
The weight of a sequence [latex]a_{0},a_{1},...,a_{n-1}[/latex] of real numbers is defined as [latex]a_{0}+a_{1}/2+...+a_{n-1}/2^{n-1}[/latex] A subsequence of a sequence is obtained by deleting some elements from the sequence, keeping the order of the remaining elements

questions.question:
The following program consists of 3 concurrent processes and 3 binary semaphores. The semaphores are initialized as S0=1, S1=0, S2=0. How many times will process P0 print '0'?

How many times will process P0 print '0'?
questions.explanation:
P0 prints once (S0 = 1), then releases S1 and S2. P1 and P2 then each release S0 once.

- If both releases happen before P0 waits again, binary S0 stays 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P0 prints once more (2 times).
- If P0 consumes the first release before the second comes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] it prints twice more (3 times).

So it prints at least twice.

Answer: At least twice

Hari(H), Gita(G), Irfan(I) and Saira(S) are siblings (i.e., brothers and sisters). All were born on 1st January. The age difference between any two successive siblings (that is born one after another) is less than three years. Given the following facts:

G and S differ by 1 year, so they are adjacent. G is not oldest and S not youngest.

- IGSH: I older than G and S older than H, so I + S [latex]\gt[/latex] G + H [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fails (i)
- IHSG: I older than H and S older than G, so I + S [latex]\gt[/latex] H + G [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fails (i)

Answer: SGHI
